entities.name: Lascaux Cave Paintings
entities.label: Evidence
entities.summary: Paleolithic cave paintings in the Dordogne region of France, dating to c. 17,000 years ago. Featuring over 600 paintings and 1,500 engravings of animals, symbols, and human figures, Lascaux is one of the most significant examples of prehistoric art. The paintings demonstrate sophisticated artistic skill, symbolic thinking, and perhaps ritual practices among Upper Paleolithic humans.
